pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIG ADVENTURE

A little dog. A big town. A ton of tricks.

Teddy is a Pembroke Welsh Corgi. He is short. He is fluffy. He has the most famous rump on the block, and he knows a ton of tricks.

His person is Doc Leo, a friendly hobo clown with a chewed-up felt fedora, wire glasses, a painted-on ash beard, a green tie and red sneakers. He walks a rubber chicken on a dog leash. Doc Leo is a proud member of the Klown Klub: he twists balloon animals, does magic tricks - there is always a dove in that hat - and marches in every parade in town. Tonight is the Klub's Big Show. Guess who the star is.

Teddy also has a big sister. Gwinn is a chocolate-brown pit-lab mix, younger than Teddy but twice his size. She was adopted, and she is still learning: she has never once sat when asked. She knows one trick, and it is zoomies. This morning Doc Leo drove ahead to the Klub in his little red CitiCar and left his costume suitcase on the back step. Gwinn found it, ran off with it, and galloped all over town. The fedora, the green tie, the red sneakers, the rubber chicken and the red nose went flying, and his balloon dogs floated away.

No nose, no show! Doc Leo is already at the Klub. Only a little dog can save the Big Show.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, yips and honks; without one, the PC speaker beeps along gamely.

A cartoon plays first: watch Gwinn make off with the suitcase (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key to get to the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around the backyard himself.

There are five stops on Teddy's adventure. Before each one, a card shows where you are, which piece of Doc Leo's costume to look for, and which trick is new. At the end of every stop, Doc Leo's friend Pockets waits with the Klown Car. Bring him the costume piece and the door pops open: hop in and he drives you to the next stop.

Energy and naps

Teddy starts with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear him down; a bone gives 25 back, and Teddy's green wobble ball is worth a whole extra nap. When his energy runs out Teddy is tuckered out and naps; he wakes at the start of the stop he was on. When all the naps are used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.
Up or WHop! Tap it for a little hop, hold it to hop higher. Let go of Up and Teddy goes back to walking, so to hop onto something, hold the arrow key toward it, press Up, and let go of Up when you are high enough.
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go. Holding Up and Right together won't do it - use Q and E, and hold them as long as you would hold Up.

How high can a corgi hop?

Two blocks easily. Three blocks if you hold Up the whole way and steer at just the right moment: Teddy scrambles up anything he can get his front paws over. Four blocks, never. Walls that tall need another way around, and there always is one.

Ledges

Awnings, branches, clotheslines, bridges and tightropes can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above.

Things that lift

Fountain jets, subway steam vents, trampolines and the Klub's stage lift push Teddy up into the air. Walk into one, ride it up, and steer off the top.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy knows a ton of tricks, and every one of them is good for something. The five he learns on the way are on the number keys along the top of the keyboard, in the order he learns them.

SpaceSpeak. WOOF! The bark rolls ahead the way Teddy faces (after a hop, it goes up). Squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese clear right out. Barking is the only thing a cat napping in a doorway respects.
DownDig. Digs up the block under Teddy's feet: bones sticking out of the lawn pop right out, and soft dirt or sawdust (look for paw prints) gives way to a tunnel underneath.
FFetch. Picks up Doc Leo's costume pieces when they are lying around. Press F while standing on one.
1High five. Teddy stands up and slaps whatever is just above his head and a little in front: a kid's hand held out, a bunch of balloons.
2Sit pretty. Sends up a heart that floats straight up two blocks. Anybody with a SIT? bubble over their head is won over.
3Spin. Twirls a little whirlwind out to each side. Revolving doors start turning (go through quick, before they stop), and people asking for a SPIN love it.
4Play dead. Hold it and Teddy flops flat as a rug. Flying discs, bowling pins and custard pies sail right over him.
5Roll over. Shakes loose a tumbleweed of corgi fluff that rolls ahead and knocks over stacks of things.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each. The F2 screen counts them as Money. Kids and klowns hand out more for a good trick.

Bones

A bone gives Teddy 25 energy and 50 points. Most of them are buried; look for one end sticking out of the ground and dig.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals floated loose from the suitcase. Three bob somewhere up high in every stop: 250 points and 10 energy each. They are never on the way; they are worth the detour.

Teddy's wobble ball

His favorite toy: green, lumpy, and it giggles when it rolls. Gwinn has it in the backyard and won't sit for anybody, but a good WOOF makes her drop it. Grab it while it wobbles: an extra nap and 500 points.

The Dog House

A tiny red library on a post in front of the blue house on Maple Street, all dog books. Hop up on the painted-rock cubby underneath: fetch (F) a book to carry along (250 points), and nose open the paw-knob drawer for dog snacks.

Root beer

Doc Leo always orders root beer. There is a stand on the Klown Klub midway: fetch him a frosty mug (500 points).

Doc Leo's costume

One piece per stop. Some are lying around and must be fetched (F); some are caught on balloons, or held by a kid who wants to see a trick first. F2 shows everything Teddy is carrying.

Backyardthe felt fedora
Maple Streetthe green tie
The parkthe red sneakers
Downtownthe rubber chicken
The Klown Klubthe red nose

Klown Klub tickets

At the Klub, the big top's turnstile takes three tickets. Doc Leo's friends give them out for tricks: Honker wants a high five, Bubbles wants a sit, and Twirly wants a spin.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Klown Klub, and Teddy's person.
  • Pockets: drives Doc Leo's little red CitiCar between stops today, with Teddy's head out of the back window. Has a pocket for everything except costume pieces.
  • Honker, Bubbles and Twirly: Klown Klub members working the midway.
  • Presto: the Klub's magician, warming up the crowd on the downtown plaza. Doves flutter out of his hat. They are harmless; just magic.
  • The parade: the Klown Klub's drummer, banner and balloon klowns, marching down Main Street toward the Big Show.
  • Juggles: a busker downtown. He means well. His bowling pins go everywhere.
  • Professor Pratfall: practices pie throws backstage, for science. Duck.
  • The kids: on porches and benches all over town. Do a trick and they share.

Pests and nuisances

  • Squirrels nip (8 energy). Bark first.
  • Cats nap in doorways and will not budge. Bark.
  • Geese guard the covered bridge in the park. Bark, from a respectful distance.
  • Pigeons peck (8 energy). Bark.
  • Flying discs, pins and pies fly at head height (8 energy each). Play dead or hop.
  • Sprinklers on Maple Street blast Teddy back where he came from. Wait for them to rest.

Gwinn

She is everywhere Teddy goes, and she leaves a mess behind her. If she bumps into Teddy she gobbles one of his treats and bolts. She was adopted and is still learning her manners: SIT means nothing to her yet, but she does listen to a bark. She is not bad. She is just Gwinn.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's Backyard

The tutorial yard: hop the garden boxes, walk the clothesline, bark at the squirrel, dig up bones, and climb the old oak (hop straight up through its branches) for the fedora. Gwinn is doing zoomies with Teddy's wobble ball: bark and she drops it. The back fence is too tall; dig under it.

2. Maple Street

The green tie is caught on yard-sale balloons under a porch roof: high five them. A cat is napping in the hedge arch, and the sprinklers come and go. Stop at the Dog House library for a book and a snack.

3. Puddlewick Park

Ride the fountain over the hedge, sit pretty for the kids on the bench (one of them has Doc Leo's red sneakers), and bark the geese off the covered bridge. Fall in the duck pond and Teddy paddles; the far bank is too high to climb out, so take the bridge.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

4. Downtown

The rubber chicken landed on a fire escape, leash and all: the subway steam vent will blow Teddy up there. Biggles Department Store is in the way and too tall to climb: spin the revolving door, go through (Gwinn is in the shoe department), and spin your way out. Under the construction shed, Juggles' pins come flying: play dead until they pass. Out on the plaza, Presto pulls doves out of his hat, and the Klown Klub parade marches down Main Street all the way to the Odeon, where the CitiCar waits.

5. The Klown Klub

Three tickets get you through the turnstile (and the root beer stand is right there on the midway). Roll a fluff ball into the bowling pins under the bleachers, play dead under the practice pies, spin through the stage door, then dig through the sawdust and ride the stage lift up. Gwinn has the red nose, in the spotlight. She won't give it up... unless somebody shows her how to sit nicely. Then the nose goes to Doc Leo, the show goes on, and afterward the whole Klub parades out into the night with Teddy riding on the CitiCar roof.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:
Credits

Design, art, music and programming: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

Pick Credits for the cast in close-up: Teddy, Gwinn, Doc Leo, the CitiCar and the Dog House, painted from life.

Starring Teddy as himself, with Gwinn as herself (sorry) and Doc Leo, the friendliest hobo clown in any klown klub, and his red 1976 CitiCar.

Built with GAME-MAKER 3.0 by Recreational Software Designs. No programming needed!

This Is Shareware

You may copy Teddy's Little Big Adventure for your friends, upload it to your favorite BBS, or put it on a shareware disk, as long as all of the files are included and unchanged.
